# Exception Handling

#### Course: Learn C++ Intermediate

## Exception Handling

As we have seen in the previous lesson, our program ends with an error message when an exception occurs.

Most of the time, rather than showing this default error message, we may want to show a more helpful custom message or run a different set of code. This is known as exception handling.

Exception handling is the process of responding to exceptions in a custom way during the execution of a program.

In C++, we use the try, throw, and catch statements to handle exceptions.

- try: It includes the block of code that can cause exceptions.
- throw: It throws an exception when an error is encountered.
- catch: It catches the exception and executes a block of code when an exception occurs.

![Idea Emoji](data:image/png;base64,)

These statements are collectively called the try...catch block. Its syntax is:

```cpp
try {
    // code that may cause exception
    // usually includes a throw statement
}
catch (arg) {
    //  code to run when exception occurs
}
```

We put the code that may raise an exception inside the try block. Now if an exception occurs, the program jumps immediately to the catch block. However, if exceptions do not occur, the catch block is skipped.

Also, notice that the catch block takes an argument arg. This argument can be of any type (int, char, string, etc.).

Next, we will see a working example of exception handling.
